newsitem.title: CHINA: China to have final word on top HK officials.
newsitem.headline: China to have final word on top HK officials.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa has the right to nominate his senior officials after the territory reverts to Chinese rule next year, but Beijing will have the final word, an official said on Tuesday.

"For senior officials, they need the nomination of the top administrative official and finally obtain appointment by the central government," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a news briefing.
"Mr Tung Chee-hwa completely has the right to nominate the senior officials he needs," he said.

Shen said he hoped Hong Kong's current line-up of officials would remain in office in Hong Kong after Beijing regains control at midnight on June 30 next year after more than 150 years of British rule.
This was important for Hong Kong's smooth transition in 1997 as well as for its future prosperity and stability, he said.
Hong Kong shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa was to fly to Beijing on Tuesday afternoon to be anointed by China's communist leadership as the territory's first post-colonial leader.
Tung, 59, who was officially named Hong Kong chief executive in waiting by Chinese Premier Li Peng on Monday, is likely to meet Chinese President Jiang Zemin on Wednesday.
Tung was selected last week by a 400-member, Beijing-controlled Selection Committee.
